# Results (all numbers generated by code from saved prediction files on Drive)

Protocol: identity-disjoint splits; checkpoint = best validation AUC; threshold = Youden J on validation only; AUC is the primary metric; paired bootstrap (1,000 resamples) for differences. One seed unless "n=3". Test sets: FF++ c23 test (140 real / 560 fake, 4 methods), Celeb-DF strict test (219 / 500, identities unseen), Celeb-DF official test (178 / 340).

## R1. Baseline and cross-dataset generalization (Model v1, n=3)

| Trained on | Tested on | AUC (mean ± std) | Bal. acc | Real recall | Fake recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FF++ | FF++ (same dataset) | **0.9716 ± 0.0022** | 0.918 | 0.902 | 0.933 |
| FF++ | Celeb-DF strict (unseen) | **0.8676 ± 0.0015** | 0.772 | 0.791 | 0.753 |
| FF++ | Celeb-DF official (unseen) | **0.8152 ± 0.0081** | 0.713 | 0.813 | 0.614 |
| Celeb-DF strict | Celeb-DF strict (same) | **0.9957 ± 0.0017** | 0.962 | 0.937 | 0.986 |
| Celeb-DF strict | FF++ (unseen) | **0.6642 ± 0.0095** | 0.570 | 0.971 | 0.168 |

The generalization gap is large and asymmetric. Celeb-DF is nearly saturated in-dataset (0.996), yet a model trained on it catches only 17% of FF++ fakes at its validation threshold. Training on the more diverse FF++ (4 methods) transfers far better (0.868).

## R2. Temporal modelling (FTCN gap): no gain

| Model | Params | FF++ | CDF strict | CDF official | Δ vs v1 on CDF strict (95% CI) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v1 mean (per-frame), seed 0 | 4.01 M | 0.9737 | 0.8689 | 0.822 | — |
| v2a BiLSTM + attention | 7.16 M | 0.9708 | 0.8522 | 0.8104 | −0.017 [−0.034, 0.000] n.s. |
| v2b temporal-difference conv | 5.06 M | 0.9691 | 0.8621 | 0.8083 | −0.007 [−0.024, +0.011] n.s. |

Neither temporal head improves in-dataset or cross-dataset AUC. Both are worse under heavy downscaling (CDF strict down64: 0.716 / 0.724 vs 0.799). Celeb-DF-trained BiLSTM: 0.9938 in-dataset, 0.6572 on FF++ (v1: 0.9957 / 0.6642).

## R3. Frequency branch (CVPR 2025 gap): significantly worse

| | FF++ | CDF strict | CDF official |
|---|---|---|---|
| v3 RGB + FFT | 0.9634 | 0.8528 | 0.8124 |
| Δ vs v1 (95% CI) | −0.010 [−0.017, −0.004] **sig.** | −0.016 [−0.034, −0.000] **sig.** | −0.009 [−0.028, +0.011] n.s. |

## R4. Unseen manipulation method (LOMO, CVPR 2025 gap)

Per-method FF++ test AUC (each method's fakes vs all real videos):

| Model | Deepfakes | Face2Face | FaceSwap | NeuralTextures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v1 (all 4 methods seen), n=3 mean | 0.9819 | 0.9742 | 0.9870 | **0.9435** |
| trained without NeuralTextures | 0.9770 | 0.9736 | 0.9904 | **0.7829** |

Holding out NeuralTextures costs **0.16 AUC** on that method only. Learned cues are method-specific, the core claim behind the CVPR 2025 generalization gap.

## R5. Mouth evidence (LipForensics gap, E2)

AUC on the FF++ test set (rows = how the model was trained, columns = what it saw at test time):

| Trained \ Tested | full face | mouth masked | mouth only |
|---|---|---|---|
| full face (v1) | **0.9737** | 0.7692 | 0.8174 |
| mouth masked | 0.8794 | **0.9085** | 0.7089 |

Full-face model, mouth masked at test time, per method: Deepfakes 0.984→0.826, Face2Face 0.976→0.705, FaceSwap 0.989→**0.924**, NeuralTextures 0.946→**0.622**.

Celeb-DF full-face model (face swap): 0.9954 → 0.9664 with the mouth masked (−0.03).

By mouth-motion tercile (full-face model, full test; n = 233–240 per group):

| | low motion | mid | high |
|---|---|---|---|
| FF++ | 0.958 | 0.967 | 0.975 |
| Celeb-DF strict | 0.998 | 0.990 | 0.996 |

**Findings.**
1. The full-face detector keeps working on low-mouth-motion videos (FF++ 0.958 vs 0.975; Celeb-DF ≥ 0.99), the condition LipForensics reports as a weakness.
2. For face swaps (FaceSwap, Celeb-DF) the evidence is spread over the face: masking the mouth costs only 0.03–0.06.
3. For mouth-region reenactment (NeuralTextures, Face2Face) the mouth is the main evidence, and occluding it is close to chance for NeuralTextures (0.62).
4. Training with the mouth masked recovers most of it (0.769 → 0.909 overall). Fakes remain detectable without any mouth pixels.

Caveats: synthetic grey box; one seed; mouth box from MTCNN mouth corners.

## R6. Compression / resolution robustness (Celeb-DF gap)

Crop-level degradation of test faces, threshold fixed from clean validation:

| Model | Test | clean | JPEG 50 | JPEG 30 | down 112 | down 64 | JPEG50+down112 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v1 | CDF strict | 0.869 | 0.827 | 0.777 | 0.841 | 0.799 | 0.783 |
| **robust** | CDF strict | **0.881** | **0.864** | **0.842** | **0.861** | **0.827** | **0.832** |
| v1 | FF++ | 0.974 | 0.943 | 0.907 | 0.929 | 0.810 | 0.889 |
| **robust** | FF++ | 0.961 | 0.932 | **0.918** | 0.923 | **0.861** | **0.896** |
| v1 (CDF-trained) | CDF strict | 0.995 | 0.991 | 0.982 | 0.993 | 0.982 | 0.984 |

Robustness augmentation (JPEG q20–90, downscale 56–160 px, blur):
- Cross-dataset: CDF official +0.022 [+0.002, +0.043] **significant**; CDF strict +0.012 [−0.005, +0.030] n.s.
- In-dataset FF++: −0.013 [−0.021, −0.007] **significant**.
- On cross-dataset JPEG 30 the drop shrinks from −0.092 to −0.039.

This is crop-level degradation, not re-encoding of the original videos.

## Final model choice (rule fixed before results)
Highest mean cross-dataset AUC among full-face FF++ models: **robust_ffpp_s0** (CDF strict 0.881, official 0.844; mean 0.863), versus v1 seed 0 at 0.845. It uses the per-frame head, so the app's frame timeline is exact.
